title: Sell Mineral Rights in Foley, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Foley, AL | Cash Offer
metaDescription: Foley, Baldwin County mineral owner with an old south Alabama oil or gas lease? We give a clear, honest cash offer with no pressure to sell.
heroLead: Foley sits inland from the Gulf beaches in south Baldwin County, an area shaped more by agriculture and, more recently, tourism development than by oil and gas activity, though old mineral reservations from the farming era still show up in local deeds.
intro: If you are a Foley property owner who discovered a mineral reservation buried in your deed, or an heir who inherited a fractional interest tied to farmland that has since been sold and redeveloped, we can help you figure out exactly what that reservation is worth today.

sections.heading: Old farmland reservations in a fast-growing area
paragraphs: As south Baldwin County has grown rapidly with resort and residential development, a lot of the original agricultural tracts around Foley changed hands multiple times, and mineral reservations from decades ago sometimes got carried forward into new deeds without the current owner fully realizing it. If you bought property here and noticed a mineral exception in your title work, that is worth investigating rather than ignoring.
On the flip side, if your family sold the surface but kept the minerals generations ago, you may still hold rights to land that looks completely different today than when the reservation was written.

sections.heading: What determines value in this part of the county
paragraphs: South Baldwin County sits at the edge of the broader south Alabama Smackover and Norphlet trend, but without dense drilling directly under most Foley-area tracts, so value here depends heavily on proximity to any actual production and current operator interest, if any, rather than an established royalty history.
We evaluate each Foley interest on its specific facts and give you an honest read on whether it is more of a long-shot speculative holding or a genuinely marketable asset.

faqs.question: My title company found a mineral exception on my Foley property. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It means someone, likely a prior owner or their heirs, reserved the mineral rights when the surface was sold, so you own the land but not what is underneath it.

faqs.question: Is there active oil and gas production near Foley?
faqs.answer: Not directly under most of the city; the broader Smackover and Norphlet trend runs through this part of south Alabama, but dense production is more concentrated elsewhere in the region.

faqs.question: Can I still sell an interest with no lease or production history?
faqs.answer: We can evaluate it, though value for undeveloped interests is necessarily more conservative than for producing ones, and we will explain our reasoning.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my family still holds a mineral interest somewhere in Foley?
faqs.answer: A title search or a review of your deed's legal description can usually answer this, and we can help interpret what you find.
